one_liner: GitHub is ready for an agent toolkit: developers can register an app under a personal account, and its public REST and GraphQL APIs cover core development workflows.

auth.notes: GitHub recommends a GitHub App for integrations acting on another user's behalf. Tokens authenticate API requests; some app endpoints require basic authentication, and public-data requests can be unauthenticated.

access.notes: The self-serve free path uses a personal account on GitHub's hosted service. The self-hosted alternative, GitHub Enterprise Server, is an Enterprise deployment. Organization owners can require approval for tokens accessing organization resources.

api.notes: The public REST and GraphQL references describe integrations and workflows. App permissions determine which operations an integration can perform.

mcp.notes: GitHub provides and maintains the server, documents a hosted remote option, and says it is available to all GitHub users regardless of plan type. Individual tools retain their underlying feature's access requirements.

verdict.rationale: A developer can register a GitHub App under a personal account and use the documented REST or GraphQL APIs. App permissions and organization approval policies may constrain access to particular resources.

problems: The free-plan documentation and app-registration documentation establish the self-serve path on separate pages; neither quoted sentence explicitly says “API credentials are included in GitHub Free.”
Organization-controlled resources may require approval even when a developer can create their own app or token.
name: GitHub

verification.note: Quotes show GitHub App user authorization and user access tokens for acting on a user's behalf, basic authentication for some app endpoints, unauthenticated public-data requests, and fine-grained personal access tokens. Nothing recommends a different primary method.

A GitHub App can be registered under a personal account, and GitHub offers free plans; no quoted payment, trial, or approval gate applies to creating that app. Enterprise Cloud and self-hosted Enterprise Server support both deployments, while organization approval is only an optional restriction on fine-grained tokens.
Public pages document both the REST and GraphQL APIs for integrations and workflows, and app permissions include read-and-write access. Nothing contradicts broad breadth.
GitHub provides, maintains, and hosts the MCP server and says it is available to all GitHub users regardless of plan. No quote labels it beta, pilot, or unlaunched.
The confirmed quote is on the Composio GitHub toolkit page and describes GitHub as the listed app.
Self-serve app registration and documented REST and GraphQL APIs with read-and-write permissions meet buildable_now with no main blocker.
